in-ncert.name: National Council of Educational Research and Training
in-ncert.description: Develops the national school curriculum framework and textbooks, and conducts the National Talent Search Examination; also houses the National Council for Teacher Education secretariat.
in-ncert.head: in-pos-director-ncert

in-ncte.name: National Council for Teacher Education
in-ncte.description: Regulates teacher-education institutions and programmes nationally — norms, recognition and standards for teacher training courses.
in-ncte.legalBasis: National Council for Teacher Education Act, 1993

in-cbse.name: Central Board of Secondary Education
in-cbse.description: India's largest school examination board, affiliating over 27,000 schools in India and abroad and conducting Class 10/12 board exams.
in-cbse.head: in-pos-chairperson-cbse

in-kvs.name: Kendriya Vidyalaya Sangathan
in-kvs.description: Runs the ~1,250-school Kendriya Vidyalaya chain for children of central-government transferable employees (plus three schools abroad), one of the world's largest school chains.
in-kvs.head: in-pos-commissioner-kvs

in-nvs.name: Navodaya Vidyalaya Samiti
in-nvs.description: Runs the Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalaya system of ~650 free, fully-residential schools for academically talented children mostly from rural areas, one per district.
in-nvs.head: in-pos-commissioner-nvs

in-nios.name: National Institute of Open Schooling
in-nios.description: The world's largest open-schooling system, offering secondary/senior-secondary and vocational certification outside the formal school system through study centres in India and abroad.
in-nios.head: in-pos-chairman-nios

in-ugc.name: University Grants Commission
in-ugc.description: Coordinates, funds and sets standards for university education in India, recognises universities and disburses grants and doctoral fellowships.
in-ugc.head: in-pos-chairman-ugc

in-aicte.name: All India Council for Technical Education
in-aicte.description: National regulator for technical, management, pharmacy and architecture education — approves and monitors AICTE-affiliated colleges and courses.
in-aicte.legalBasis: All India Council for Technical Education Act, 1987

in-nta.name: National Testing Agency
in-nta.description: Conducts national entrance examinations for higher education (JEE Main, NEET-UG, UGC-NET, CUET and others); stopped conducting recruitment exams from 2025 after repeated paper-leak controversies.
in-nta.head: in-pos-dg-nta

in-naac.name: National Assessment and Accreditation Council
in-naac.description: Assesses and accredits Indian higher-education institutions on an eight-grade scale; in Feb 2025 the CBI arrested its chairman and several inspection-committee members in a bribery-for-accreditation scandal, after which NAAC suspended implicated assessors and reviewed hundreds of past assessments.

in-nirf.name: National Institutional Ranking Framework
in-nirf.description: Annual methodology and ranking exercise (not a standalone body) run by the Ministry of Education / National Board of Accreditation to rank Indian higher-education institutions across 11+ categories.

in-iits.name: Indian Institutes of Technology
in-iits.description: Network of 23 autonomous public engineering/technology Institutes of National Importance, governed jointly through the IIT Council (chaired ex officio by the Education Minister).
in-iits.notes: All 23 IITs as of 2026-09-25: IIT Kharagpur; IIT Bombay; IIT Kanpur; IIT Madras; IIT Delhi; IIT Guwahati; IIT Roorkee; IIT Jodhpur; IIT Hyderabad; IIT Gandhinagar; IIT Ropar; IIT Patna; IIT Bhubaneswar; IIT Indore; IIT Mandi; IIT (BHU) Varanasi; IIT Palakkad; IIT Tirupati; IIT (ISM) Dhanbad; IIT Bhilai; IIT Dharwad; IIT Jammu; IIT Goa.

in-iims.name: Indian Institutes of Management
in-iims.description: Network of 22 autonomous public business schools declared Institutes of National Importance, coordinated through the IIM Coordination Forum with full operational autonomy since the IIM Act 2017.
in-iims.notes: All 22 IIMs as of 2026-09-25: IIM Calcutta; IIM Ahmedabad; IIM Bangalore; IIM Lucknow; IIM Indore; IIM Kozhikode; IIM Shillong; IIM Raipur; IIM Ranchi; IIM Rohtak; IIM Kashipur; IIM Tiruchirappalli; IIM Udaipur; IIM Amritsar; IIM Bodh Gaya; IIM Nagpur; IIM Sambalpur; IIM Sirmaur; IIM Visakhapatnam; IIM Jammu; IIM Mumbai; IIM Guwahati.

in-nits.name: National Institutes of Technology
in-nits.description: Network of 32 centrally-funded technical Institutes of National Importance (list includes IIEST Shibpur), coordinated through the NIT Council.
in-nits.legalBasis: National Institutes of Technology, Science Education, and Research Act, 2007
in-nits.notes: All 32 NITs/NIT-equivalents as of 2026-09-25: NIT Karnataka (Surathkal); NIT Warangal; MANIT Bhopal; IIEST Shibpur; VNIT Nagpur; NIT Durgapur; NIT Jamshedpur; NIT Srinagar; NIT Silchar; MNNIT Allahabad; SVNIT Surat; NIT Calicut; NIT Rourkela; MNIT Jaipur; NIT Kurukshetra; NIT Tiruchirappalli; NIT Hamirpur; NIT Jalandhar; NIT Patna; NIT Raipur; NIT Agartala; NIT Arunachal Pradesh; NIT Delhi; NIT Goa; NIT Manipur; NIT Meghalaya; NIT Mizoram; NIT Nagaland; NIT Puducherry; NIT Sikkim; NIT Uttarakhand; NIT Andhra Pradesh.

in-central-universities.name: Central Universities of India
in-central-universities.description: India's 57 central (Union-government-established/funded) universities, established mostly under individual Acts of Parliament and funded through the UGC.
in-central-universities.legalBasis: Individual Acts of Parliament per university; funded via UGC Act, 1956
in-central-universities.notes: All 57 institutions Wikipedia's 'Central university (India)' list groups as central universities as of 2026-09-25 (a few, e.g. National Sports University, Indian Maritime University, are technically separate Institutions of National Importance rather than UGC-Act central universities, but are centrally administered on the same footing): Central Tribal University of Andhra Pradesh; Central University of Andhra Pradesh; National Sanskrit University; Rajiv Gandhi University; Assam University; Tezpur University; Central University of South Bihar; Mahatma Gandhi Central University; Nalanda University; Dr. Rajendra Prasad Central Agriculture University; Guru Ghasidas Vishwavidyalaya; Central Sanskrit University; Indira Gandhi National Open University; Jamia Millia Islamia; Jawaharlal Nehru University; Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri National Sanskrit University; South Asian University; University of Delhi; Central University of Gujarat; Gati Shakti Vishwavidyalaya; Central University of Haryana; Central University of Himachal Pradesh; Central University of Jammu; Central University of Kashmir; Central University of Jharkhand; Central University of Karnataka; Central University of Kerala; Sindhu Central University; Dr. Hari Singh Gour University; Indira Gandhi National Tribal University; Mahatma Gandhi Antarrashtriya Hindi Vishwavidyalaya; Central Agricultural University; Manipur University; National Sports University; North Eastern Hill University; Mizoram University; Nagaland University; Central University of Odisha; Pondicherry University; Central University of Punjab; Central University of Rajasthan; Sikkim University; Central University of Tamil Nadu; Indian Maritime University; English and Foreign Languages University; Maulana Azad National Urdu University; University of Hyderabad; Sammakka Sarakka Central Tribal University; Tripura University; Aligarh Muslim University; University of Allahabad; Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar University; Banaras Hindu University; Rajiv Gandhi National Aviation University; Rani Lakshmi Bai Central Agricultural University; Hemwati Nandan Bahuguna Garhwal University; Visva-Bharati University.

in-min-women-and-child-development.name: Ministry of Women and Child Development
in-min-women-and-child-development.description: Runs India's women's-welfare and child-protection policy and schemes: anganwadi nutrition services (Poshan/ICDS), adoption regulation, child protection, and women's safety and empowerment programmes.
in-min-women-and-child-development.legalBasis: Government of India (Allocation of Business) Rules, 1961
in-min-women-and-child-development.head: in-pos-minister-women-and-child-development

members.title: Minister of State in the Ministry of Women and Child Development

budget.source: https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/index.php (Union Budget 2026-2027 portal, Ministry of Finance, Govt of India; verified budget presented 1 Feb 2026 by FM Nirmala Sitharaman)

in-cara.name: Central Adoption Resource Authority
in-cara.description: Nodal statutory body regulating in-country and inter-country adoption of Indian children, and India's Central Authority under the 1993 Hague Adoption Convention.
in-cara.legalBasis: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015

in-nipccd.name: National Institute of Public Cooperation and Child Development
in-nipccd.description: Apex training, research and documentation institute for child development and women's-empowerment programmes, with regional centres in Guwahati, Bengaluru, Lucknow and Indore.

in-poshan-abhiyaan.name: Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 (POSHAN Abhiyaan)
in-poshan-abhiyaan.description: India's flagship nutrition mission, delivered through ~1.4 million Anganwadi Centres nationwide, providing supplementary nutrition, pre-school education and health referral for children under 6 and pregnant/lactating mothers; merged the erstwhile ICDS scheme with the National Nutrition Mission in 2021-22 as 'Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0'.

in-rashtriya-mahila-kosh.name: Rashtriya Mahila Kosh
in-rashtriya-mahila-kosh.description: Provides micro-credit to poor women, mainly through NGOs/SHG-federation intermediaries, for income-generation activities.

in-min-social-justice-and-empowerment.name: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
in-min-social-justice-and-empowerment.description: Runs welfare, protection and economic-empowerment policy for Scheduled Castes, Other Backward Classes, senior citizens, Safai Karamcharis and persons with disabilities, through two departments.
in-min-social-justice-and-empowerment.legalBasis: Government of India (Allocation of Business) Rules, 1961
in-min-social-justice-and-empowerment.head: in-pos-minister-social-justice-and-empowerment

members.title: Minister of State in the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
Minister of State in the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment

budget.source: https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/index.php (Union Budget 2026-2027 portal, Ministry of Finance, Govt of India; verified budget presented 1 Feb 2026 by FM Nirmala Sitharaman)

in-dept-social-justice-and-empowerment.name: Department of Social Justice and Empowerment
in-dept-social-justice-and-empowerment.description: Handles welfare and development schemes for Scheduled Castes, Other Backward Classes, senior citizens and Safai Karamcharis.

budget.source: https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/index.php (Union Budget 2026-2027 portal, Ministry of Finance, Govt of India; verified budget presented 1 Feb 2026 by FM Nirmala Sitharaman)

in-dept-empowerment-of-persons-with-disa.name: Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities
in-dept-empowerment-of-persons-with-disa.description: Administers disability-rights law and welfare schemes, including the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 and the Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities.
in-dept-empowerment-of-persons-with-disa.legalBasis: Government of India (Allocation of Business) Rules, 1961; department created 2012

budget.source: https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/index.php (Union Budget 2026-2027 portal, Ministry of Finance, Govt of India; verified budget presented 1 Feb 2026 by FM Nirmala Sitharaman)

in-nsfdc.name: National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation
in-nsfdc.description: Government-owned non-profit corporation providing concessional finance and skill-training support for economic empowerment of Scheduled Caste families below double the poverty line.

in-nbcfdc.name: National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation
in-nbcfdc.description: Government-owned non-profit corporation providing concessional finance for self-employment and skill development of persons from Other Backward Classes and denotified/nomadic tribes.

in-nskfdc.name: National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation
in-nskfdc.description: Government-owned corporation providing concessional finance and self-employment/rehabilitation support for Safai Karamcharis (sanitation workers), manual scavengers and their dependants.

in-ncsk.name: National Commission for Safai Karamcharis
in-ncsk.description: Investigates conditions of Safai Karamcharis (sanitation/manual-scavenging workers) and recommends welfare programmes; currently a non-statutory body periodically extended by government resolution rather than under its lapsed 1993 Act.
in-ncsk.legalBasis: Constituted 1994 under NCSK Act, 1993 (Act lapsed Feb 2004; body since continued by executive resolution)
in-ncsk.head: in-pos-chairperson-ncsk

in-nisd.name: National Institute of Social Defence
in-nisd.description: Training and research institute on 'social defence' issues — drug-demand reduction, elder care, and welfare of persons in need of care and protection.

in-ambedkar-foundation.name: Dr. Ambedkar Foundation
in-ambedkar-foundation.description: Runs commemorative, scholarship and welfare schemes in memory of B. R. Ambedkar, including international/national Ambedkar award schemes and the Mahaparinirvan Diwas observance.

in-ccpd.name: Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities
in-ccpd.description: Quasi-judicial office safeguarding the rights of persons with disabilities and adjudicating individual grievances under the disability-rights law; historically held ex officio by the DEPwD Secretary.
in-ccpd.legalBasis: Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016
in-ccpd.head: in-pos-ccpd

in-min-tribal-affairs.name: Ministry of Tribal Affairs
in-min-tribal-affairs.description: Nodal ministry for welfare and development of Scheduled Tribes — education (EMRS), livelihoods and minor-forest-produce marketing (TRIFED), and concessional finance (NSTFDC).
in-min-tribal-affairs.legalBasis: Government of India (Allocation of Business) Rules, 1961; created as separate ministry 1999
in-min-tribal-affairs.head: in-pos-minister-tribal-affairs

members.title: Minister of State in the Ministry of Tribal Affairs

budget.source: https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/index.php (Union Budget 2026-2027 portal, Ministry of Finance, Govt of India; verified budget presented 1 Feb 2026 by FM Nirmala Sitharaman)

in-nstfdc.name: National Scheduled Tribes Finance and Development Corporation
in-nstfdc.description: Apex government-owned corporation providing concessional finance and skill upgradation support for the economic development of Scheduled Tribes, channelised through State Channelizing Agencies.

in-trifed.name: Tribal Cooperative Marketing Development Federation of India
in-trifed.description: National apex cooperative body for marketing tribal minor forest produce and handicrafts (via the 'Tribes India' brand and Van Dhan Yojana), and for fair-price procurement support to tribal gatherers.

in-nests.name: National Education Society for Tribal Students
in-nests.description: Society that manages the Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRS) — fully residential CBSE-affiliated schools for Scheduled Tribe students, targeting one EMRS per block with ≥50% ST population and ≥20,000 tribal persons.

in-ntri.name: National Tribal Research Institute
in-ntri.description: Apex research institute for tribal affairs, coordinating a network of State Tribal Research Institutes on tribal culture, ethnography and policy research.

in-min-minority-affairs.name: Ministry of Minority Affairs
in-min-minority-affairs.description: Nodal ministry for welfare, education and economic-empowerment schemes for India's notified minority communities (Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists, Parsis, Jains), and administers Waqf and Haj matters.
in-min-minority-affairs.legalBasis: Government of India (Allocation of Business) Rules, 1961; created as separate ministry 2006
in-min-minority-affairs.head: in-pos-minister-minority-affairs

members.title: Minister of State in the Ministry of Minority Affairs

budget.source: https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/index.php (Union Budget 2026-2027 portal, Ministry of Finance, Govt of India; verified budget presented 1 Feb 2026 by FM Nirmala Sitharaman)

in-nmdfc.name: National Minorities Development and Finance Corporation
in-nmdfc.description: Government-owned non-profit corporation providing concessional finance for self-employment and income-generation activities for people from notified minority communities.

in-central-waqf-council.name: Central Waqf Council
in-central-waqf-council.description: Statutory advisory body to the Union Government on Waqf-Board administration and proper management of Waqf (Islamic charitable-endowment) properties across State Waqf Boards.
in-central-waqf-council.legalBasis: Waqf Act, 1995, as amended by the Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025

in-haj-committee.name: Haj Committee of India
in-haj-committee.description: Statutory body organising and facilitating the annual Haj pilgrimage to Saudi Arabia for Indian Muslims, acting as nodal agency for State Haj Committees.

in-maef.name: Maulana Azad Education Foundation
in-maef.description: Registered society running scholarship and educational-infrastructure schemes for educationally backward minority communities.

in-min-labour-and-employment.name: Ministry of Labour and Employment
in-min-labour-and-employment.description: Sets labour law and social-security policy (the four consolidated Labour Codes), and runs employees' provident fund and health-insurance schemes, mines safety regulation and industrial-relations machinery.
in-min-labour-and-employment.legalBasis: Government of India (Allocation of Business) Rules, 1961
in-min-labour-and-employment.head: in-pos-minister-labour-and-employment

members.title: Minister of State in the Ministry of Labour and Employment

budget.source: https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/index.php (Union Budget 2026-2027 portal, Ministry of Finance, Govt of India; verified budget presented 1 Feb 2026 by FM Nirmala Sitharaman)

in-epfo.name: Employees' Provident Fund Organisation
in-epfo.description: Administers India's mandatory retirement provident-fund, pension and insurance schemes for organised-sector employees (firms with 20+ workers), through the Central Board of Trustees; among the world's largest social-security organisations by membership.
in-epfo.legalBasis: Employees' Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952 (now folded into the Code on Social Security, 2020)
in-epfo.head: in-pos-cpfc-epfo

in-esic.name: Employees' State Insurance Corporation
in-esic.description: Administers India's health-insurance and cash-benefit social-security scheme for organised-sector workers below a wage ceiling, running its own network of ESIC hospitals, dispensaries and medical colleges.
in-esic.head: in-pos-dg-esic

in-dge.name: Directorate General of Employment
in-dge.description: Compiles national employment-market information and runs the National Career Service portal connecting job-seekers, employers and skilling/career-counselling services.

in-dgms.name: Directorate General of Mines Safety
in-dgms.description: Regulates occupational safety, health and welfare of workers in coal, metalliferous and oil mines under the Mines Act, 1952; headquartered in Dhanbad.

in-clc.name: Office of the Chief Labour Commissioner (Central)
in-clc.description: Central enforcement machinery for labour laws (minimum wages, industrial disputes, contract labour) in central-sphere establishments, and chief conciliation authority for central-sphere industrial disputes.

in-vvgnli.name: V. V. Giri National Labour Institute
in-vvgnli.description: Apex labour-research, training and policy institute (formerly the Central Labour Institute), named after former President V. V. Giri.

in-labour-bureau.name: Labour Bureau
in-labour-bureau.description: Statistical wing of the ministry, compiling India's labour-market data — Consumer Price Index for Industrial/Agricultural/Rural Workers, employment-unemployment surveys and wage-rate indices.

in-min-skill-development-and-entrepreneu.name: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
in-min-skill-development-and-entrepreneu.description: Runs India's vocational-training and skilling policy (Skill India Mission), industrial training institutes, apprenticeship regulation and entrepreneurship-promotion programmes.
in-min-skill-development-and-entrepreneu.legalBasis: Government of India (Allocation of Business) Rules, 1961; created as separate ministry 2014
in-min-skill-development-and-entrepreneu.head: in-pos-minister-skill-development-and-entrepreneurship

budget.source: https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/index.php (Union Budget 2026-2027 portal, Ministry of Finance, Govt of India; verified budget presented 1 Feb 2026 by FM Nirmala Sitharaman)

in-nsdc.name: National Skill Development Corporation
in-nsdc.description: Not-for-profit public-private-partnership company (51% private, 49% government-held) that funds and catalyses private-sector vocational-training capacity, sector skill councils and skilling partnerships.

in-ncvet.name: National Council for Vocational Education and Training
in-ncvet.description: Regulates vocational-education and skill-training institutions and awarding bodies, formed in 2018 by merging the National Council for Vocational Training (NCVT) and National Skill Development Agency (NSDA).
in-ncvet.head: in-pos-chairperson-ncvet

in-dgt.name: Directorate General of Training
in-dgt.description: Runs India's public Industrial Training Institute (ITI) system, apprenticeship-training scheme, and vocational-instructor training (Craftsmen/Apprentices Training Schemes).

in-niesbud.name: National Institute for Entrepreneurship and Small Business Development
in-niesbud.description: Apex training and research body for entrepreneurship development and small-business promotion, running Entrepreneurship Development Programmes nationally.

in-nia-ayurveda.name: National Institute of Ayurveda
in-nia-ayurveda.description: Deemed-to-be university (De-novo category, since 2020) for Ayurveda teaching, clinical training and research; one of AYUSH's flagship national institutes.

in-cbwe.name: Central Board for Workers Education
in-cbwe.description: Runs worker-education, trade-union leadership and labour-literacy training programmes for organised- and unorganised-sector workers through regional/sub-regional centres.

in-indian-institutes-of-skills.name: Indian Institutes of Skills
in-indian-institutes-of-skills.description: A small, growing network of flagship, industry-partnered vocational-training institutes (modelled loosely on the IIT/IIM brand) — the first opened in Mumbai (with Tata Group) in 2022, followed by further IIS in Kanpur, Ahmedabad, Bhubaneswar and Faridabad.

in-min-science-and-technology.name: Ministry of Science and Technology
in-min-science-and-technology.description: Umbrella ministry comprising three departments — Science & Technology (DST), Biotechnology (DBT), and Scientific & Industrial Research (DSIR) — that fund and steer India's civilian scientific research, biotech and industrial R&D ecosystem.
in-min-science-and-technology.legalBasis: Government of India (Allocation of Business) Rules, 1961
in-min-science-and-technology.head: in-pos-mos-science-and-technology-1

budget.source: https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/index.php (Union Budget 2026-2027 portal, Ministry of Finance, Govt of India; verified budget presented 1 Feb 2026 by FM Nirmala Sitharaman)

in-dept-science-and-technology.name: Department of Science and Technology
in-dept-science-and-technology.description: Formulates national science & technology policy, funds basic and applied research, autonomous S&T institutes, and national missions (e.g. National Quantum Mission) through grants to universities and institutions.
in-dept-science-and-technology.legalBasis: Government of India (Allocation of Business) Rules, 1961
in-dept-science-and-technology.head: in-pos-mos-science-and-technology-1

budget.source: https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/index.php (Union Budget 2026-2027 portal, Ministry of Finance, Govt of India; verified budget presented 1 Feb 2026 by FM Nirmala Sitharaman)

in-dept-biotechnology.name: Department of Biotechnology
in-dept-biotechnology.description: Administers development and commercialisation of modern biology and biotechnology in India, funding research institutes, biotech startups (via BIRAC) and national biotech missions.
in-dept-biotechnology.legalBasis: Government of India (Allocation of Business) Rules, 1961
in-dept-biotechnology.head: in-pos-mos-science-and-technology-1

budget.source: https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/index.php (Union Budget 2026-2027 portal, Ministry of Finance, Govt of India; verified budget presented 1 Feb 2026 by FM Nirmala Sitharaman)

in-dept-scientific-and-industrial-resear.name: Department of Scientific and Industrial Research
in-dept-scientific-and-industrial-resear.description: Promotes industrial R&D, recognises in-house R&D units of companies, and administers CSIR as its operating arm; the DSIR Secretary is concurrently Director General of CSIR.
in-dept-scientific-and-industrial-resear.legalBasis: Government of India (Allocation of Business) Rules, 1961
in-dept-scientific-and-industrial-resear.head: in-pos-mos-science-and-technology-1

budget.source: https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/index.php (Union Budget 2026-2027 portal, Ministry of Finance, Govt of India; verified budget presented 1 Feb 2026 by FM Nirmala Sitharaman)

in-csir.name: Council of Scientific and Industrial Research
in-csir.description: India's largest chain of publicly funded industrial & applied-science R&D institutions; runs a nationwide network of national laboratories covering chemistry, metallurgy, aerospace, drugs, food tech, genomics and more.
in-csir.legalBasis: Registered society (Societies Registration Act, 1860); Prime Minister is ex-officio President
in-csir.hq: Anusandhan Bhawan, 2 Rafi Marg, New Delhi
in-csir.head: in-pos-dg-csir

stats.note: commonly cited as ~37-39 constituent national laboratories plus outreach centres; count varies by source/year

in-anrf.name: Anusandhan National Research Foundation
in-anrf.description: Apex body created to seed, grow and promote research and innovation across India's universities, colleges and R&D institutions; absorbed the Science and Engineering Research Board (SERB) as a division. Governing Board is chaired by the Prime Minister; an Executive Council (chaired by the PM's Principal Scientific Adviser) runs day-to-day functioning.
in-anrf.head: in-pos-prime-minister
in-anrf.notes: Governing Board first met 2024-09-10; CEO name not confirmed by an available 2025-2026 source in this research pass.

in-serb.name: Science and Engineering Research Board
in-serb.description: Former statutory body that funded basic research in science and engineering; dissolved in 2023 and its functions absorbed into ANRF. Retained here as a historical/legacy record since its brand and schemes still operate as an ANRF vertical.
in-serb.notes: Dissolved 2023, functions merged into ANRF. Not a currently independent legal entity.

in-birac.name: Biotechnology Industry Research Assistance Council
in-birac.description: Not-for-profit Section-8 public sector enterprise that funds and mentors biotech startups and early-stage biotech industry R&D through grants, seed funds and incubators.
in-birac.legalBasis: Companies Act (Section 8 company), Department of Biotechnology initiative

in-dst-autonomous-institutes.name: DST Autonomous Institutes (aggregate)
in-dst-autonomous-institutes.description: Aggregate record for the ~20+ autonomous R&D and science-outreach institutes funded and administered by DST (e.g. S.N. Bose National Centre for Basic Sciences, Raman Research Institute, Wadia Institute of Himalayan Geology, Vigyan Prasar, National Innovation Foundation), each with its own governing body and director.
in-dst-autonomous-institutes.notes: Aggregate placeholder per research scope; individual institutes not separately itemised in this pass except Vigyan Prasar, NIF and Survey of India below.

in-vigyan-prasar.name: Vigyan Prasar
in-vigyan-prasar.description: Autonomous DST body for popularising science, producing science-communication content, and running the National Science Day and Rashtriya Vigyan Evam Prodyogiki Sanchar Parishad outreach network.

in-national-innovation-foundation.name: National Innovation Foundation - India
in-national-innovation-foundation.description: Autonomous DST body that scouts, documents and helps commercialise grassroots technological innovations and traditional knowledge from across India.

in-survey-of-india.name: Survey of India
in-survey-of-india.description: India's national mapping agency and the government's principal adviser on surveying, geodesy and cartography; headed by the Surveyor General of India.
in-survey-of-india.head: in-pos-surveyor-general-india

in-nii.name: National Institute of Immunology
in-nii.description: Autonomous DBT research institute (National Institute of Immunology), part of India's public biotechnology research network.
in-nii.legalBasis: Registered society under Department of Biotechnology

in-nccs.name: National Centre for Cell Science
in-nccs.description: Autonomous DBT research institute (National Centre for Cell Science), part of India's public biotechnology research network.
in-nccs.legalBasis: Registered society under Department of Biotechnology

in-nbrc.name: National Brain Research Centre
in-nbrc.description: Autonomous DBT research institute (National Brain Research Centre), part of India's public biotechnology research network.
in-nbrc.legalBasis: Registered society under Department of Biotechnology

in-rgcb.name: Rajiv Gandhi Centre for Biotechnology
in-rgcb.description: Autonomous DBT research institute (Rajiv Gandhi Centre for Biotechnology), part of India's public biotechnology research network.
in-rgcb.legalBasis: Registered society under Department of Biotechnology

in-ils.name: Institute of Life Sciences
in-ils.description: Autonomous DBT research institute (Institute of Life Sciences), part of India's public biotechnology research network.

in-com-jpc-one-nation-one-election.name: Joint Committee on the Constitution (One Hundred and Twenty-Ninth Amendment) Bill, 2024 and the Union Territories Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2024
aliases: JPC on One Nation One Election
in-com-jpc-one-nation-one-election.description: Examines the Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill, 2024 and the Union Territories Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2024, which together propose to hold simultaneous ('one nation, one election') elections to the Lok Sabha and all State Legislative Assemblies. Introduced in Lok Sabha 17 December 2024 and referred to this JPC on 19 December 2024; enlarged to 39 members (27 Lok Sabha + 12 Rajya Sabha) after cross-party demands. As of September 2026 the JPC is still consulting stakeholders (including state Chief Ministers) and has not yet presented its report; chairman P. P. Chaudhary has indicated it is examining feasibility for the 2029 general elections.
in-com-jpc-one-nation-one-election.legalBasis: Motion of reference adopted by both Houses of Parliament (Joint Committee on a Bill)

aliases: JPC on Removal of Arrested Ministers
in-com-jpc-removal-of-ministers-130th-am.description: Examines bills that would provide for the automatic removal of a Prime Minister, Chief Minister or other Minister (including in Delhi, Puducherry and Jammu & Kashmir) who is arrested and held in custody for 30 consecutive days on a serious criminal charge. Introduced in Lok Sabha on 20 August 2025 and referred to this JPC the same day. As of September 2026 the bills remain with the JPC; no report has been presented.

in-com-jpc-fcra-amendment-2026.name: Joint Committee on the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026
in-com-jpc-fcra-amendment-2026.description: Examines the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, which creates a framework for supervision, management and disposal of foreign contributions/assets of organisations that cease to hold an FCRA certificate. Introduced in Lok Sabha 25 March 2026; referred to this JPC (per PRS bill-track status) 12 August 2026. As of September 2026 the bill remains in committee. Chairperson not independently confirmed from a public source as of research date.
in-com-jpc-fcra-amendment-2026.legalBasis: Motion of reference adopted by both Houses of Parliament (Joint Committee on a Bill)

in-com-jpc-waqf-amendment-2024.name: Joint Committee on the Waqf (Amendment) Bill, 2024
in-com-jpc-waqf-amendment-2024.description: Examined the Waqf (Amendment) Bill, 2024. Introduced in Lok Sabha 8 August 2024 and referred to this JPC the same day; the JPC presented its report on 30 January 2025. The Bill (incorporating the JPC's recommendations) was passed by Lok Sabha on 2 April 2025 and by Rajya Sabha on 3 April 2025, enacted as the Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025. The JPC's mandate is concluded; it is not active as of September 2026.
in-com-jpc-waqf-amendment-2024.legalBasis: Motion of reference adopted by both Houses of Parliament (Joint Committee on a Bill)

in-lok-sabha.name: Lok Sabha
in-lok-sabha.description: The directly-elected lower house of Parliament; 543 members elected from single-member territorial constituencies by universal adult suffrage. The Union Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to it. Current term: 18th Lok Sabha, constituted after the 2024 general election.

in-parliament.name: Parliament of India
in-parliament.description: The bicameral national legislature of India, comprising the President, the Lok Sabha (House of the People) and the Rajya Sabha (Council of States). It makes Union and concurrent-list laws and holds the Union Council of Ministers accountable.

in-lok-sabha-secretariat.name: Lok Sabha Secretariat
in-lok-sabha-secretariat.description: The permanent administrative and procedural secretariat that services the Lok Sabha, under the overall direction of the Speaker; headed by the Secretary-General.
in-lok-sabha-secretariat.head: in-pos-secretary-general-lok-sabha

in-rajya-sabha.name: Rajya Sabha
in-rajya-sabha.description: The upper house of India's bicameral Parliament. Members are indirectly elected by the elected members of State and Union Territory Legislative Assemblies (single transferable vote), plus 12 nominated by the President for contributions to art, literature, science and social service. It is a permanent body, not subject to dissolution, with one-third of members retiring every two years.
in-rajya-sabha.head: in-pos-chairman-rajya-sabha

in-rajya-sabha-secretariat.name: Rajya Sabha Secretariat
in-rajya-sabha-secretariat.description: Permanent administrative and procedural staff of the Rajya Sabha, under the overall direction and control of the Chairman, headed by the Secretary-General. Provides secretarial, research, legislative-drafting and committee support to the House.
in-rajya-sabha-secretariat.head: in-pos-secretary-general-rajya-sabha

in-rbi.name: Reserve Bank of India
in-rbi.description: India's central bank; regulates banks, NBFCs and payment systems, conducts monetary policy, manages the currency and India's foreign-exchange reserves.
in-rbi.head: in-pos-governor-rbi

in-rbi-mpc.name: Monetary Policy Committee
in-rbi-mpc.description: Six-member statutory committee that sets India's benchmark policy interest rate to meet the inflation target set by the Government.
in-rbi-mpc.legalBasis: Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, Chapter III-F (s.45ZB), inserted by the Finance Act, 2016
in-rbi-mpc.head: in-pos-governor-rbi

holder.name: Surya Kant
holder.notes: 53rd CJI. Born 1962-02-10 at Hisar, Haryana. Was Chief Justice of the Himachal Pradesh High Court (elevated to that post 2018-10-05) before elevation as a Supreme Court judge on 2019-05-24; earlier a permanent judge (2004) and Advocate General (2000) of Haryana at the Punjab & Haryana High Court. Original record's 'Justice Dinesh Kumar' (no since-date, generic Economic-Times citation from 2013) was almost certainly a stale/incomplete name for the SAME person now more fully identified as P. S. Dinesh Kumar -- not a different, unconfirmed individual.

in-pos-chairman-ugc.name: Chairman, UGC
in-pos-chairman-ugc.title: Chairman, UGC

holder.name: Deepti Gaur Mukerjee
holder.notes: Higher Education Secretary holding ADDITIONAL CHARGE as UGC Chairperson since ~August 2026 (when she became Higher Education Secretary). This continues a chain of bureaucrats holding the post on additional charge: M. Jagadesh Kumar's term as UGC Chairman ended ~April 2025; Vineet Joshi (then Higher Education Secretary) held additional charge from April 2025 until his August 2026 transfer to the Panchayati Raj ministry; Mukerjee succeeded him in both roles. Academics and a former UGC secretary have publicly criticised this as violating UGC Act s.4, which bars serving government officers from the chairmanship. The Vice-Chairperson post is also vacant. Original entry (M. Jagadesh Kumar) was STALE by ~17 months as of the 2026-09-25 as-of date — he left in April 2025.

st-an.name: Andaman and Nicobar Islands
st-an.description: An archipelago Union Territory in the Bay of Bengal comprising the Andaman and Nicobar island groups; administered directly by the Union through a Lieutenant Governor, with no state legislature. Home to protected tribal groups (Sentinelese, Jarawa, Onge, Shompen) under the Andaman and Nicobar Islands (Protection of Aboriginal Tribes) Regulation.

governor.title: Lieutenant Governor of Andaman and Nicobar Islands
governor.name: Prof. (Dr.) Dinesh Sharma

budget.source: https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/index.php (Union Budget 2026-2027 portal, Ministry of Finance, Govt of India; verified budget presented 1 Feb 2026 by FM Nirmala Sitharaman)

st-ap.name: Andhra Pradesh
st-ap.description: Andhra Pradesh is a state of India with its capital at Amaravati.

st-ar.name: Arunachal Pradesh
st-ar.description: A Himalayan border state in India's Northeast bordering Bhutan, China (disputed McMahon Line) and Myanmar; became a full state in 1987 after being a Union Territory. Governed under a Governor-Chief Minister system with a single-chamber legislature.

st-as.name: Assam
st-as.description: Assam is a State of India with its capital at Dispur.

st-br.name: Bihar
st-br.description: A state in eastern India, India's second most populous state (2011 census) and its most densely populated large state; capital Patna. Governed under the standard Governor–Council of Ministers model with a bicameral legislature (Assembly + Legislative Council).

st-ch.name: Chandigarh
st-ch.description: A Union Territory and the joint capital of Punjab and Haryana, planned by Le Corbusier; has no legislature of its own and is administered directly by an Administrator appointed by the Union, an office held ex officio by the Governor of Punjab since 1984.

budget.source: https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/index.php (Union Budget 2026-2027 portal, Ministry of Finance, Govt of India; verified budget presented 1 Feb 2026 by FM Nirmala Sitharaman)

st-cg.name: Chhattisgarh
st-cg.description: A mineral-rich, heavily forested state in central India carved out of eastern Madhya Pradesh in November 2000, with Raipur as its capital.

st-dh.name: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
st-dh.nameHi: दादरा और नगर हवेली और दमन और दीव
st-dh.description: A Union Territory on India's west coast formed on 26 January 2020 by merging the former UTs of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and of Daman and Diu; administered directly by the Union through an Administrator, with no state legislature. Silvassa is the largest city; the territory elects two Lok Sabha members from separate Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu constituencies.

governor.title: Administrator of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
governor.name: Praful Khoda Patel

budget.source: https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/index.php (Union Budget 2026-2027 portal, Ministry of Finance, Govt of India; verified budget presented 1 Feb 2026 by FM Nirmala Sitharaman)

st-dl.name: Delhi
st-dl.description: A union territory with a partial state legislature; the seat of the Government of India. Administered jointly by an elected Legislative Assembly/Council of Ministers (with subjects other than police, public order and land) and a Lieutenant Governor representing the Union.

budget.source: https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/index.php (Union Budget 2026-2027 portal, Ministry of Finance, Govt of India; verified budget presented 1 Feb 2026 by FM Nirmala Sitharaman)

st-ga.name: Goa
st-ga.description: India's smallest state by area, on the west coast; a former Portuguese colony merged into India in 1961 and made a full state in 1987.

st-gj.name: Gujarat
st-gj.description: Western coastal state, India's leading industrial and port state, with the longest coastline of any state.

st-hr.name: Haryana
st-hr.description: A north Indian state carved out of the eastern, Hindi-speaking part of the former Punjab state in 1966; surrounds Delhi on three sides and shares the city of Chandigarh with Punjab as its capital.

st-hp.name: Himachal Pradesh
st-hp.description: Himalayan state in north India; capital Shimla (summer), winter capital Dharamshala. Full statehood in 1971.

st-jk.name: Jammu and Kashmir
st-jk.description: A union territory with its own elected legislature, formed on 31 October 2019 from the reorganisation of the former State of Jammu and Kashmir. The Lieutenant Governor retains control of police, public order and All India Services; the elected government handles other subjects. Statehood restoration has been promised but not yet enacted as of September 2026.

governor.title: Lieutenant Governor of Jammu and Kashmir
governor.name: Manoj Sinha

budget.source: https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/index.php (Union Budget 2026-2027 portal, Ministry of Finance, Govt of India; verified budget presented 1 Feb 2026 by FM Nirmala Sitharaman)

st-jh.name: Jharkhand
st-jh.description: A mineral-rich state in eastern India carved out of southern Bihar in 2000; capital Ranchi.

st-ka.name: Karnataka
st-ka.description: Karnataka is a state of India with its capital at Bengaluru.

st-kl.name: Kerala
st-kl.description: A southwestern Indian state on the Malabar Coast, known for its high human-development indicators; capital Thiruvananthapuram, legislature elected every five years.

st-la.name: Ladakh
st-la.description: A union territory without a legislature, formed on 31 October 2019 from the bifurcation of the former State of Jammu and Kashmir. Administered directly by a Lieutenant Governor appointed by the President; local governance is via two Autonomous Hill Development Councils (Leh and Kargil). Subject of an active statehood / Sixth Schedule protection movement through 2025-2026. Districts figure of 7 reflects 5 new districts (Changthang, Drass, Nubra, Sham, Zanskar) reportedly carved out in 2026 in addition to the original Leh and Kargil districts (1979) — recent and should be re-verified against an official notification.

budget.source: https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/index.php (Union Budget 2026-2027 portal, Ministry of Finance, Govt of India; verified budget presented 1 Feb 2026 by FM Nirmala Sitharaman)

st-ld.name: Lakshadweep
st-ld.description: India's smallest Union Territory, a chain of coral atolls in the Arabian Sea off the Kerala coast; administered directly by the Union through an Administrator, with no state legislature. Almost entirely populated by Scheduled Tribes; its sole Lok Sabha seat is ST-reserved.

budget.source: https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/index.php (Union Budget 2026-2027 portal, Ministry of Finance, Govt of India; verified budget presented 1 Feb 2026 by FM Nirmala Sitharaman)

st-mp.name: Madhya Pradesh
st-mp.description: India's second-largest state by area, in central India; known as the 'heart of India', with Bhopal as capital and Indore as its largest city.

st-mh.name: Maharashtra
st-mh.description: India's second-most populous state and its largest state economy; home to Mumbai, the country's financial capital.

st-mn.name: Manipur
st-mn.description: A Northeast Indian state bordering Myanmar, home to the Meitei-majority Imphal Valley and surrounding Naga/Kuki-Zo hill districts. President's Rule (Article 356) was in force from 13 February 2025 to 4 February 2026 following ethnic violence and the resignation of CM N. Biren Singh; an elected government resumed office on 4 February 2026.

st-ml.name: Meghalaya
st-ml.description: A Northeast Indian state carved out of Assam in 1972, home to the matrilineal Khasi, Jaintia and Garo peoples. Most of the state is Sixth Schedule tribal area governed in part by three Autonomous District Councils alongside the elected state government.

st-mz.name: Mizoram
st-mz.description: Northeastern Indian state bordering Myanmar and Bangladesh, predominantly Mizo (Christian, tribal) population; a former Union Territory that became a full state in 1987 under the 1986 Mizoram Peace Accord.

st-nl.name: Nagaland
st-nl.description: Northeastern Indian state bordering Myanmar, home to numerous Naga tribes; formed in 1963 as India's 16th state, subject to special protections under Article 371A.

st-od.name: Odisha
st-od.description: A state on India's eastern coast; capital Bhubaneswar. Governed under the standard Governor-Council of Ministers model with a unicameral legislature.

st-py.name: Puducherry
st-py.description: A Union Territory with its own elected legislature and Council of Ministers (per Article 239A), made up of four non-contiguous regions: Puducherry, Karaikal, Mahe and Yanam.

budget.source: https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/index.php (Union Budget 2026-2027 portal, Ministry of Finance, Govt of India; verified budget presented 1 Feb 2026 by FM Nirmala Sitharaman)

st-pb.name: Punjab
st-pb.description: A northwestern Indian state bordering Pakistan, formed on a linguistic basis in 1966 out of the former Punjab state (Haryana and Himachal Pradesh were carved out separately); shares its capital Chandigarh with Haryana as a Union Territory.

st-rj.name: Rajasthan
st-rj.description: India's largest state by area, in the northwest, dominated by the Thar Desert, with Jaipur ('the Pink City') as its capital.

st-sk.name: Sikkim
st-sk.description: Sikkim is a State of India with its capital at Gangtok.

st-tn.name: Tamil Nadu
st-tn.description: A southern Indian state on the Coromandel Coast; the 6th-most populous state, with Chennai as its capital and a legislature elected every five years.

st-tg.name: Telangana
st-tg.description: Telangana is a state of India with its capital at Hyderabad.

st-tr.name: Tripura
st-tr.description: Northeastern Indian state bordering Bangladesh on three sides; a former princely state that merged with India in 1949 and became a full state in 1972.

st-up.name: Uttar Pradesh
st-up.description: India's most populous state, in the Indo-Gangetic plain of north India; capital Lucknow. Sends the largest contingent to the Lok Sabha (80 seats) of any state.

st-uk.name: Uttarakhand
st-uk.description: Himalayan state carved out of Uttar Pradesh in 2000; legislative capital Bhararisain (Gairsain), seat of government at Dehradun. Known as 'Devbhoomi' for its Hindu pilgrimage sites.

st-wb.name: West Bengal
st-wb.description: West Bengal is a State of India with its capital at Kolkata.
